title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short technical verification lemma. The facing pages are typescript of SGA 7 IX (Néron models, Thm 5.4) on reused paper and are unrelated.

Objects:
- A_n° = S{X_0,...,X_{n-1}} is the divided-power (Γ) polynomial algebra over the base S, in n variables.
- A_n = S{U_0,...,U_{n-1}}[dU_0,...,dU_{n-1}] is the divided-power de Rham complex of the PD-polynomial algebra. It is Γ_S(U_0,...,U_{n-1}) tensored with the exterior algebra on the dU_r.
- The change of variables X_0 = U_0 and X_k = U_k − U_{k-1} identifies A_n° ≅ S{U_0,...,U_{n-1}}. This is a triangular, unimodular change of coordinates, so it extends to divided powers.
- Each factor S{U_r} is presented as an algebra by generators U_{r,i} = U_r^{(i)} (i ≥ 1, with U^{(0)} = 1) and relations U_{r,i}U_{r,j} = c_{ij}U_{r,i+j}, where c_{ij} = binom(i+j, i). This presentation is valid over Z, since Γ(X) is free on the X^{(i)} with that multiplication table.

The maps σ_r:
- σ_r: A_1 → A_n (written A_*σ_r) is the functorial map induced by the r-th coordinate map. It sends X_0 to U_r, so σ_r^*(X_0^{(i)}) = U_r^{(i)}.
- These are presumably the cosimplicial or coordinate structure maps of the system n ↦ A_n.

The argument:
- Suppose one is given a family φ_n: A_n° → A_n compatible with the structure maps. Naturality forces φ_n(U_r^{(i)}) = σ_r^*(φ_1(X_0^{(i)})) = σ_r^*(ξ_i).
- Here ξ_i = φ_1(X_0^{(i)}) ∈ A_1 has the general form Σ_j a_ij U^{(j)} + (Σ_j b_ij U^{(j)}) dU.
- Uniqueness of φ_n is therefore immediate.
- For existence, G. defines φ_n° by U_r^{(i)} ↦ ξ_{r,i} := σ_r^*(ξ_i). He checks the defining relations: ξ_{r,i}ξ_{r,j} = σ_r^*(ξ_iξ_j) = σ_r^*(c_{ij}ξ_{i+j}) = c_{ij}ξ_{r,i+j}. This uses that σ_r^* is a ring homomorphism and that the ξ_i satisfy the relations in A_1, because φ_1 is a homomorphism. He writes 'OK'.

Purpose: this is part of showing that a natural operation (an algebra endomorphism or transformation) between the PD-polynomial functor and the PD de Rham complex is determined by its value in one variable, and conversely extends. That is a step in studying the structure, possibly cosimplicial, of the divided-power de Rham complex.
errors: Possible gap: A_n° is a tensor product of the one-variable algebras S{U_r}. Checking the relations inside each factor separately is enough only if the images of different factors commute in A_n. A_n is graded-commutative, and the ξ_{r,i} can have a degree-1 part (Σ b_ij U^{(j)} dU_r). The odd parts for different r anticommute, so ξ_{r,i}ξ_{s,j} − ξ_{s,j}ξ_{r,i} = 2·(odd)(odd'). This need not vanish unless the b_ij vanish, 2 = 0, or one works with graded tensor products. The page does not address this.
Minor: degree-0 components (X^{(0)} = 1 ↦ 1) and unitality are left implicit.

Divided-power de Rham complex of a PD polynomial algebra, A_n = Γ(U_0..U_{n-1}) ⊗ Λ(dU_0..dU_{n-1})

ideas.what: A natural transformation on PD-polynomial algebras in n variables is determined by its value on one variable via the coordinate maps σ_r
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda / determination of natural operations by the one-variable case

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification inside a larger construction on divided-power de Rham complexes. Nothing new beyond the context, and there is a small unaddressed commutativity point.

'l'unicité de φ_n' is plausible; the phrase reads roughly 'On connaît ainsi l'unicité de φ_n, et que on devra avoir'.
The crossed-out superscript on U_{r,i} in the first displayed formula is a struck '(i)'.
The sentence 'Il y a [-un-] {+donc+} hom. d'algèbres {+unique+} A_n° → A_n' is correct, with the target written ᴬA_n or A_n.
